newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Media & Advertising Digest - July 16.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Media & Advertising Digest - July 16.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Britain's biggest cider maker, H.P. Bulmer Holdings Plc, will show no profits growth next year due to a big increase in its advertising budget, a spokesman says. Bulmer will increase its investment in ads to 8.0 million pounds ($13.4 million) in the year to April 1998 from from 4.7 million pounds in the 1997 financial year.

FRANKFURT - The co-owner of German advertising agency Tostmann & Wulfes, Tom Tostmann, confirms his partner, Thomas Wulfes, is considering leaving the agency and that they are discussing a possible sell-off. "We are talking about the future," Tostmann says, adding he expects a final decision about Wulfes' future with the agency to be reached in the next two days.

NEW YORK - Advertising group McCann-Erickson Worldwide has formed a new agency network called Thunder House Online Marketing Communications. It will capitalise on the growing business of on-line advertising and commerce.

LONDON - Media Business Group, one of the UK's leading media independents, announces it has been awarded a new media buying contract for Cable & Wireless Communications. The contract is expected to gross about 50 million pounds.

NASHVILLE, Tennessee - Service Merchandise Co Inc says it expects to shift about $4 million, on an after-tax basis, of advertising expenses that were incurred in last year's fourth quarter into the third quarter this year. The company expects to launch a television and insert advertising campaign in the third quarter directed towards placing a greater emphasis on new customers.

LONDON - Britain's Advertising Standards Authority, the industry's self-regulating body, celebrates its 35-year history with the publication of a booklet that shows how advertising standards have changed. Adverts highlighted include ads for an MG Midget car and for Max Factor lipstick, both of which used phallic imagery and underscore the changes in how women have been targeted and portrayed in advertising, the ASA says.

BETHESDA, Maryland - Snyder Communications Inc, which provides targeted marketing solutions, says it has bought Sampling Corp of America and British-based Bounty Group Holdings Ltd. Sampling Corp provides targeted sampling programs for large companies while Bounty Group is a product sampling company focused on new mothers.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - A leading ITV executive urges the British government to cut the 400 million pound annual bill which ITV's 15 members pay the treasury. The ITV companies pay for their broadcast licences with a fixed annual cash sum plus a percentage of advertising and sponsorship revenue.
WASHINGTON- U.S. President Bill Clinton will begin seeking technology-based solutions to shield children from the seamier side of cyberspace say officials.
NEW YORK - New York Times Co says second quarter and to year-to-date advertising volume for the New York Times and Boston Globe newspapers has increased.

FRANKFURT - German newspapers saw a slight fall in the number of readers because of increasing competition from magazines over the last year, an advertising industry study by Allensbach Market and Advertising Media Analysis says.
SANTA CLARA, California - Yahoo! Inc says it and Viacom Inc.'s MTV Networks will launch MTV/Yahoo! unfURLed, a guide to music on the World Wide Web.
BERLIN - U.S. media company Metromedia International Inc has taken over Berlin talk radio station NewsTalk 93.6, the German station says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

CHICAGO - Heavy competition in the U.S. fast-food market and an unsuccessful marketing campaign took a bite out of McDonald's Corp second-quarter earnings, which are expected to rise only about seven percent, analysts say.

LONDON - British companies Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc say that Bernard Arnault, the French entrepreneur who controls conglomerate LVMH, has outlined a new proposal to both companies during talks. The companies have pledged to look closely at it.

INGOLSTADT, Germany - Audi AG, the luxury car unit of Volkswagen AG, says sales of its top-model A8 sedan surged in the first half of the year. It says sales in Germany rose 13 percent to about 3,800 vehicles during the period from January to June.

JOHANNESBURG - Tough trading conditions in the European canned fruit market and internal worries are likely to hit South Africa's Del Monte Royal Foods Ltd when it reports its interim earnings next week, analysts say.
BANGKOK - Sales of passenger cars and commercial vehicles in Thailand dropped 24.3 percent in June to 36,503 units from 48,220 in the same month last year, Toyota Motors (Thailand) says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

FRANKFURT - After years when Germans avoided movie theatres in droves, the cinema is enjoying a heyday not seen in almost two decades, a study released by the Institute of Opinion Polling says. More than seven percent of Germans over 14 years old see a movie at least once a week, it says.
BOSTON - Designers Tommy Hilfiger and Ralph Lauren have signed licensing deals with footwear companies to offer a fashionable alternative to sneakers, say industry experts.
